subject: Career
title: International Salary Differences
description: A fast breakdown of International Salary Differences for builders.

hook.text: A software engineer earns $150K in San Francisco and $60K in Berlin. Same skills, different markets.

buildup.text: Location-based pay reflects cost of living, local supply and demand, and tax structures.

discovery.text: Remote work is creating tension: should a remote worker in Lisbon earn SF rates?

twist.text: Some companies pay 'location-agnostic.' Others apply regional bands. Know which before you negotiate.

climax.text: If relocating or going remote internationally, calculate net pay — taxes and benefits shift dramatically.

punchline.text: Same job, different zip code, different paycheck.

quiz.question: Why do salaries differ significantly by location for the same role?
options: Cost of living, supply/demand, and tax structures
Companies in different countries are random

details.summary: Salary expectations vary dramatically by country due to differences in cost of living, purchasing power parity, tax structures, social benefits, and cultural negotiation norms. Professionals working globally or considering relocation must understand these factors to evaluate offers accurately.
details.whyItMatters: A $100,000 salary means very different things in San Francisco, Berlin, and Singapore. International literacy prevents costly career decisions based on nominal numbers alone.
takeaways: Purchasing power parity matters more than raw salary figures
Social benefits like healthcare and pensions offset lower base pay
Tax structures dramatically affect take-home pay across countries

faq.question: How do I compare salaries between countries with different currencies?
faq.answer: Use purchasing power parity calculators rather than simple currency exchange rates. PPP adjusts for what your salary can actually buy locally. Also factor in tax rates, mandatory social contributions, and employer-provided benefits like healthcare.

faq.question: Why are tech salaries so much higher in the United States than Europe?
faq.answer: US tech salaries reflect higher cost of living in tech hubs, fewer mandatory employer benefits, at-will employment risk, and venture capital culture that prioritizes talent acquisition. European salaries are lower nominally but include benefits that reduce total compensation gaps.
